chunks: From him, from Faḍālah, from Ibn Muskān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If a man sleeps or forgets to perform the maghrib and the later ʿishaʾ prayer, then if he wakes before fajr with enough time to perform both of them, he should perform them both. But if he fears that one of them will escape him, then he should begin with the later ʿishaʾ. And if he wakes after fajr, then he should begin and perform the ṣubḥ prayer, then maghrib, then ʿishaʾ before sunrise.

key_terms.الْعِشَاءَ الْآخِرَةَ: the later night obligatory prayer, ʿishaʾ
key_terms.الْفَجْرِ: dawn, marking the beginning of fajr time
key_terms.طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ: sunrise, the limit mentioned here for completing the sequence

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone slept through or forgot maghrib and ʿishaʾ and woke up near fajr?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who missed maghrib and ʿishaʾ due to sleep or forgetfulness and then woke near the time of fajr. It explains the order of prayers depending on whether there is enough time before fajr or only enough time to preserve one prayer, and it instructs that if one wakes after fajr, ṣubḥ is performed first, followed by the missed prayers before sunrise.
